name: delete the piece two words share and join the rest
one_line: Two words are printed, the letters where they meet are read off rather than guessed, and what is left of each joins into a third.
how: Print four columns — first word, second word, the key, the total — and five rows of pairs whose end and start overlap: sole and letto, luce and cena, carne and nero, pane and netto, pelo and loro. The key is read off the two printed words, so nothing here needs a dictionary. Say that a key taken too long or too short gives no total at all. Then one row where the shared piece is kept instead of thrown away: sole and letto give sotto when it goes and soletto when it stays, and one pair teaches that better than a definition. Close by asking for LUNA to be taken apart backwards, and why it cannot be.

knobs.effect: Kept, the shared letters are written once and the total is longer. Thrown away, they go from both words and the total is shorter. The same pair does both, which is why one pair is worth two examples.

Straight, the key is found by looking at the two printed words and the sheet checks itself. Reversed, a key of one letter always works as well and gives nonsense, so the checking goes back into a dictionary.

knobs.knob: which end of each word carries it
knobs.effect: Head of the first and tail of the second, and one set of three words can be asked three ways round. Each of the other three combinations of head and tail gives one question only.
Two letters make the overlap visible and the total short. One letter is available on almost any pair and settles nothing. Three or more leaves too little of either word to join.

where_the_work_is: In finding the five pairs, which is a search inside words and is where the hours go. Once they are printed the solving needs no dictionary at all, and that is rare in this chapter.
breaks: It prints. Scanned back it reads if the four columns are ruled, since a key written between columns is unreadable. On 800x480 one row of four columns fits and five do not, and five is what makes the sheet. The pairs cannot be produced by a model: it returns pairs whose ends do not overlap at all, and only writing them out letter by letter catches that.
